notes:
Account snapshot: Oxley Bridgeworks -- mid-market SaaS (product analytics + embedded insights). Evaluated Redwood Hosted API in Q4 2024 during proof-of-concept (embedded search + chat assistants). Good success on quality; want cost predictability and lower unit economics for scale -> moving to Dedicated procurement.

Key contacts (Oxley):
- Sarah Patel (Head of Product, decision owner)
- Miguel Torres (Platform Lead, technical owner)
- Jenna Park (Finance, procurement lead)

Redwood team: AE Priya Sharma, SE Lucas Chen, Solutions architect (ad-hoc) Naomi Li.

Timeline / recent activity (choppy CRM notes):
- 2024-11-20: initial discovery call; product goals: embed chat + semantic search in-app (mobile + web). latency target: p95 < 250ms for chat, 10ms-50ms for embeddings retrieval (on caching layer). cost sensitivity: high; target < $0.02 per 1k inference tokens for high-throughput paths.
- 2024-12-05: Hosted API demo (Priya + Lucas). Ran sample workload (20k queries/day) — quality + hallucination rate acceptable. Customer asked about candidate open models and quantized variants.
- 2025-01-08: POC kickoff on Hosted with 30-day trial credits. Fireflies: ff_2025-01-22_oxley-demo-1. Collected latency histograms and token counts.
- 2025-01-22: POC review; engineering: "Hosted good for early stage but unit cost too high at scale". Request: Dedicated capacity quote and commitment options.
- 2025-02-07: Pricing deep-dive with Redwood finance/solutions (ff_2025-02-07_pricing-call). Discussed commit tiers, burst mechanics, overtime/overage pricing, ramp schedule.
- 2025-02-10: Security review kickoff (SEC-1198). Provided SOC2 docs + KMS integration notes. Customer asked for audit log retention policy and regional residency details.

Use-case & technical reqs (short bullets):
- Primary workloads: chat assistants (multi-turn), embeddings for semantic search, reranking of candidate results.
- Latency/throughput: chat p95 < 250ms for 75% of traffic; expect 200 qps at peak within 12 months; embeddings batch throughput target 1k reqs/min.
- Model preferences: prefer open Llama-family / LLMs verified by Redwood; need option to route to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical routes.
- Routing/fallback: automatic fallback to smaller model family when Dedicated capacity saturated; prefer region-based routing (US East primary, EU for EU customers).
- Security: SSO/SAML integration mandatory, data residency for EU-sourced customers, KMS support for key management, audit logs available for 12 months.

POC metrics & outcome:
- Hosted POC (30d): avg token cost (hosted) = ~$0.035 per 1k tokens for generation-heavy workloads; peak p95 latency met for small batches but variance at scale.
- Internal eval: team concluded Dedicated provides 40-60% cost savings at expected scale but requires 6-12 week provisioning and ramp plan.

Pricing / packaging conversation (details captured):
- Customer requests 12-month Dedicated commitment. Baseline ask: reserved pool equivalent to 4x A100-class GPUs (continuous) with 2x burst capability for short windows.
- Preferred billing: monthly invoice with annual commitment discount. Finance (Jenna) prefers predictable monthly run-rate vs. large up-front capex.
- Commit levels discussed: 4 GPU baseline (12-month) vs. staged ramp: month1-3 -> 2 GPUs reserved, month4-6 -> 3 GPUs, month7+ -> 4 GPUs. Need formal ramp schedule in SOW.
- Burst policy: allow 2x burst for up to 8 hours/day with prioritized queueing. Overage pricing options: option A = flat 1.5x committed rate; option B = true usage at on-demand rate (higher). Oxley leaning to capped multiplier (option A) to simplify forecasting.
- Overage caps & credits: request for safety net credits for first 90 days of ramp (1% of committed spend) if provisioning delays occur.
- SLA asks: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated endpoint; guaranteed mean p95 latency targets or credit schedule. Also asked about fallback to Hosted with transparent routing and invoicing during incidents.

Negotiation points outstanding (short):
- Exact committed GPU-hour pricing per month (pending Redwood pricing sheet v3).
- Legal: termination clauses, early ramp adjustments, and overage caps.
- Technical: confirmation of KV cache sharing policies across customer instances and whether prefix caching can be reserved per tenant.
- Security: ENCRYPTED S3 access pattern for logs and KMS integration details (responses in /drive/security/oxley_security_faq.md).

Action items / next steps (choppy):
- Redwood to produce Dedicated SOW + pricing scenario A/B by 2025-02-20 (Priya lead).
- SE Lucas to validate burst queueing behavior and provide microbenchmark results for 4x A100 profile by 2025-02-18.
- Oxley finance to confirm preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. annual) and sign off on forecast by 2025-02-28.
- Legal sync: exchange redlines; schedule call week of 2025-03-03.

Quotes & paraphrases from calls:
- Sarah: "We need predictable unit economics to lock in feature pricing to customers — can't have wild swings from Hosted costs." 
- Miguel: "If we can get 40% cost saving vs Hosted and a clear ramp path, Dedicated is a no-brainer." 
- Jenna: "Monthly invoices with ramp smoothing is our preference. Large upfront committed cash is harder to justify for FY25." 

Risk notes (one-liners):
- Ramp delay risk if procurement drags -> may force temporary hybrid (Hosted + Dedicated) with complicated invoicing.
- Security sign-off timeline could push close beyond forecast month.

Internal RD/Deal strategy suggestions (AE/SE notes):
- Offer two-tier pricing: immediate discounted baseline for 12-month commit + graded discounts as commit increases. Include explicit burst multiplier option (1.5x) and an alternative on-demand fallback for extreme spikes.
- Provide a 60-90 day ramp credit to mitigate provisioning risk and accelerate legal sign-off.
- Bundle Redwood Optimize consultation (one-off) to tune batching/quantization and commit to modeled unit cost estimates.

CRM terse next line: "Procurement engaged — pricing SOW pending. Monitor SEC-1198 & INF-3221. Push for March close."
